title: Know every story in a release reaches code
statement: As a developer, I can see that every story in a release has code references, so a release claims only work we can point to in the code.
overview: Trevor's direction: it is fine to have fixes with no story, as long as every story in a release has code references. What counts decides how strict that is. Of this Saga's 24 accepted stories, `query traceability` reaches slide Item code for 13. The other 11 are the shipped Plans stories: 4 name code on their own Task, and all 11 have test-case evidence, so only counting tests lets all 24 pass. That query also covers only accepted stories, while a release can link a proposed one, so this check needs its own walk.

acceptance_criteria.statement: `release status` and the release's page name each of its stories that no current code reference reaches.
A story with no code references can be linked while a release is being prepared, since planned work has no code yet.
Marking a release released is refused while any of its stories has no code reference, and the refusal names them.
An internal note marked as a fix, with no story, is not asked for code references.
A code reference counts when it is current and reaches the story through a slide Item, a Task, or a test case's evidence.
